free_tier.stated: No free tier. NAT-512-LXC is USD 7.70 a year, printed as 'Starting from $7.70 USD Annually'; the group page showed '6 Available'.

retention.stated: annual prepay; the terms state 'After an invoice becomes 1 day past due, all services affiliated with the invoice are subject to immediate suspension and will be terminated after 3 days past due'

egress.terms: 550 GB a month at 500 Mbps on NAT-512-LXC, in the vendor's decimal unit; the page states 'Port speed limited to 1Mbps after traffic exceeded'

interface_detail: LXC guest with root; 20 IPv4 NAT ports managed from a NAT panel in the product detail page, plus an IPv6 subnet reachable on all ports
tooling: any SSH client; the WHMCS client area; no API documented on the pages read
chaining: a low-end NAT box with a real /64 that answers on every port, which makes it a WireGuard endpoint and an IPv6-reachable service host, at USD 0.64 a month on annual prepay

limits.value: 550 GB a month, then the port is limited to 1 Mbps
20 IPv4 NAT ports, for example 30101-30120, allocated from a NAT panel; all other ports are unreachable over public IPv4

binding_note: 20 forwarded IPv4 ports is the whole inbound budget over IPv4, and the vendor states the public IPv4 is blocked by the GFW by default, so in practice every reachable service has to go over the IPv6 address.

identity_cost.detail: a WHMCS account; the about page lists the payment rails as 'Alipay, UnionPay and USDT', which means no international credit card is strictly required and UnionPay is a card network. Any authorisation hold and the full accepted-card list were not published on the pages read. No ID document is requested on the registration form fields read.

reliability_note: the vendor advertises 'No surprise shutdowns - Going over quota slows you down instead'; no uptime figure or SLA was published on the pages read; no reliability event observed
confidence_note: price, shape, traffic allowance, port count, IPv6 subnet, stock count and the GFW note are quoted from the vendor's own group page read; the 20-port rule and the all-ports IPv6 rule are quoted from the vendor's own Chinese-language knowledgebase article read; the entity is corroborated by RIPEstat and PeeringDB, not by a state register. The cart could not be priced: every cart.php route resolved to the LA CN2 GIA group, including a deliberately invalid pid, so that redirect is a property of the route.

notes: The stock is real and stated: 6 Available on the group page today, which is more than most rows can say. USD 7.70 a year is USD 0.6417 a month, and 512 MB with a /64 and all ports open over IPv6 is the second-best shape per dollar found after CrockyHost. The caveat is the one the vendor prints itself: 'IPv4 is blocked by GFW by defaults, please use IPv6'. The 20-port rule is confirmed in the vendor's own knowledgebase with an example range, and the same article says IPv6 answers on any port. What is not established: whether the 20 forwarded IPv4 ports carry UDP, because the knowledgebase article read mentions only TCP conditions and never names UDP; the accepted card types beyond UnionPay; any authorisation hold; and whether ByteVirt LLC appears in the Missouri state register, because every route to the Missouri Secretary of State search timed out or returned the search form rather than a result. The LLC name is corroborated by an allocated AS holder name in RIPEstat and by a PeeringDB organisation record, which is stronger than a website claim but is not a state register. That is the same gap the corpus has already been burned by once, so the row carries it openly rather than closing it.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 7.70 a year / 12 = USD 0.6417 a month. VPS billing: the machine bills whether it runs or not, so the 10 h/day and 24/7 figures are identical. The money out of pocket is USD 7.70 once a year.
extras.renewal_usd: not published separately; the ladder shows one annual price and no renewal column

network_out.ports: 20 IPv4 NAT ports from a panel range such as 30101-30120; the IPv6 subnet answers on all ports

extras.udp: not stated for the IPv4 ports: the vendor's knowledgebase article names only TCP conditions and never says UDP. The same article states 'IPv6 支持全端口开放' (IPv6 supports all ports open), which carries UDP by construction.
